items.why: The report says I_D/I_G rises 0.247→0.569→1.192 and D' 'appears and grows with dose', while G FWHM stays at 13.56–14.15 cm⁻¹ and 2D at 'FWHM 32.1, 32.1, 31.9 cm⁻¹'; it treats doses 1–3 with the stage-1 relation and concludes the 'only thing changing is disorder'.
Using peak heights it gives 'L_D ≈ 24.2, 15.9, 11.0 nm' for I_D/I_G 0.247, 0.569, 1.192; the prefactor ranges (20.5–27.3, 13.5–18.0, 9.3–12.4 nm) fall within the rubric ranges.

It writes the relation explicitly as 'L_D = sqrt(1.8e-9 · λ⁴ / (I_D/I_G)) with λ = 532 nm (λ⁴ = 8.0e10 nm⁴)', so it uses the wavelength dependence rather than 514.5 nm constants; it does not separately say that the same ratio gives a different L_D at another laser line.

It notes that dose 4 has a lower I_D/I_G (0.56–0.76), broad G/D (45–65 cm⁻¹) and the '2D band nearly gone', and says 'the apparent drop from dose 3 to dose 4 must not be read as healing' and that the relation is not valid there; it does not give L_D < 3 nm explicitly, and it calls dose 4 amorphisation rather than stage 2.
It reports 'I_D/I_D' = 6.1±2, 6.1±0.6, 6.9±0.3' as 'closer to a vacancy-like' signature, citing Eckmann values '≈13 sp³, ≈7 vacancy, ≈3.5 boundary'; it does not state the low-density validity limit.
It clearly says it uses peak heights ('height ratio I_D/I_G') and also reports area ratios (0.243, 0.609, 1.255), though it does not say Cançado's relation is calibrated on heights.

It asks 'What is dose in physical units (ion species, energy and fluence; laser exposure; electron dose)?', but only to fit a dose law, not because the point-defect relation and the D/D' ratio depend on defect type.

wrong_claims.why: It explicitly says the dose-4 drop 'must not be read as healing' and gives dose 4 no L_D ('not valid for dose4').
It uses λ = 532 nm in the λ⁴ relation.
It treats the 2154.1 cm⁻¹ feature as 'one cosmic spike removed (dose 2, 2154.1 cm⁻¹, +7160 counts)'.

items.why: The report says "G and 2D both red-shift monotonically with laser power" and both broaden, notes Si "shows no measurable power-dependent shift", and concludes "Laser heating is the most consistent explanation."
It uses chi_G = -0.016 cm-1/K to get "1.78 cm-1 / 0.016 cm-1/K = 111 K" between 0.5 and 5 mW, but gives no 2 mW value and no cross-check from 2D with about -0.034 cm-1/K.

It computes the 2D/G ratio as "about 2.9" and compares it with Lee 2012's strain slope of about 2.2, saying "strain cannot be separated from heating"; but it does not state clearly that the heating trajectory follows the strain line, so a naive vector analysis would misread heating as strain.

It recommends "Trust the 0.5 mW spectrum for position analysis: it is the least heated", gives a P=0 extrapolated intercept (1581.45), and says strain cannot be separated from heating across the powers.

It asks for "the spot size" and whether power is measured at the sample, but it proposes a repeat 0.5 mW measurement to test reversibility rather than a lower-power measurement to confirm the linear, heating-free regime.

It uses 0.5 mW as the reference and says "G value of about 1581.3 cm-1 ... is consistent with near-neutral graphene", but it refuses to assess strain from the absolute positions and does not compare 2D (2669.5) with the unstrained reference.

wrong_claims.why: It attributes the shifts to heating, says "Doping is not supported", and treats strain only as an unseparable upper bound; it does not attribute the power dependence to strain or doping.
It says "The 5 mW spectrum is the least trustworthy" and recommends 0.5 mW.

items.why: The report states "Au: G 1580.3... 2D 2681.1" and "Cu: G 1579.6... 2D 2695.4" and concludes "Both spectra show graphene-like sp2 carbon" with monolayer-like I2D/IG on both metals.

It gives "Au: D at 1344.4... ID/IG height = 0.95" and for Cu "D fitted at 1348±5... Height ratio 0.53-0.69... undetermined rather than low", which matches about 1 vs about 0.6 with the Cu value poorly constrained.
The report never mentions the authors' hypothesis that strain from rapid solidification of the droplet causes the stronger D band on Au.

It notes that the D band may come from "edges, wrinkles or amorphous carbon" and that strain and doping need a G-2D correlation, but it never says outright that D needs defects to activate while strain only shifts G and 2D.
It asks "What laser wavelength was used?... it fixes the D and 2D dispersion, the L_D estimate, and whether the 2D position indicates strain or doping".
It says "Signal-to-noise on Cu is marginal... D band is near the noise", calls the Cu G FWHM "poorly constrained", gives error bars, and calls the Cu D/G "undetermined".

wrong_claims.why: The report gives "L_D_nm: Au ~4-6 nm for 514-633 nm excitation (assumed, wavelength not recorded)", a quantitative L_D from an assumed wavelength, even though it is caveated.
The report never attributes the Au D band to strain, and it leaves the strain sign as "none determined".

items.why: The report states flake 2 sits at "1369.0 ± 0.25 cm⁻¹, about 2.8 cm⁻¹ above flake 1 (1366.2 …)", that "flake 2 is broader (22 vs 18 cm⁻¹)", and that "Monolayer hBN is consistent with this (E2g upshift and broadening…)".

It says position alone is not conclusive ("few-layer flakes give similar signatures", "an E2g line alone cannot identify a monolayer"), but it never gives the small 2–4 cm⁻¹ size of the upshift or the ±2 cm⁻¹ sample-to-sample variation.

It names strain as a possible cause ("The +2.8 cm⁻¹ upshift in flake 2 could come from thickness, strain or interface effects"), but never mentions cleavage-induced redshifts of 1–2 cm⁻¹ or that they dominate in bilayers.

It reports the much weaker signal ("area ratio 0.105") and gives linear scaling with layers only as a hypothesis ("If E2g intensity were linear in layer number, N2 ≈ 0.105 × N1"), but it calls intensity "not a calibrated thickness scale" and never says intensity is the more useful measure once calibrated.

It recommends "AFM step height on flake 2, a same-spot Raman calibration against a flake of known thickness", and it explicitly checks normalisation against the Si 520 line, concluding that line is unreliable for these two spectra and asking for a same-session calibration.

wrong_claims.why: The report states "Raman alone cannot establish that it is a monolayer" and "monolayer neither confirmed nor excluded".
The report says nothing about the bilayer shift direction and does not claim bilayers upshift like monolayers.

items.why: The report gives raw shifts of "E2g ... diff +2.51; A1g ... diff +2.44 cm^-1" and says the separation "is unchanged" (21.58 vs 21.51 cm^-1), which is within range of the rubric's ~21.4 cm^-1.

The report states "the Si 520 cm^-1 reference moved by the same amount (+2.49 cm^-1)", going from 519.977 to 522.469, and attributes it to "a spectrometer wavenumber calibration difference rather than a sample change."
After Si referencing the positions "agree to within 0.05 cm^-1" within the fit error, but the report reads Delta ≈ 21.5 cm^-1 as "roughly in the 3-5 layer range" rather than a bilayer.

The report concludes "Nothing in these spectra supports adsorbate doping or strain" and says the linewidths are unchanged, but it never gives the diagnostic signatures (electron doping softens and broadens A1g; strain shifts E2g much more than A1g) and only says both modes "respond to doping and strain."
The report asks "Was the spectrometer recalibrated, or the grating or centre wavelength changed, between the two days? Was a Si reference measured with each spectrum?"

wrong_claims.why: The report rejects strain and doping as explanations ("strain_sign: none detectable", "doping_type: none detectable") and attributes the shift to calibration.
The report states the flake "did not thin, oxidise or change layer count" and finds no defect features on either day.

items.why: The report gives the trend directly: bulk-like flakes 'sit near E2g ≈ 383, A1g ≈ 408; B is closer to the monolayer side (E2g higher, A1g lower)', and its Δ ladder grows with layer number.

Flake B at 'Δ 19.23' is called '1L, possibly 2L' (correct), but flake A at 21.45 is assigned 'about 3–4 layers' rather than bilayer, and the report never says the 1L-to-2L step is the most robust distinction.

C (25.06) and D (24.27) are called 'bulk-like' and the report says 'Δ cannot separate their layer numbers' (bounded, not counted), but the bound is '≥6' with saturation at '5–6 layers' instead of about 4, and C being thicker is only implied by the Si/E2g ordering.

The report rejects intensity as a thickness proxy and mentions '285 nm SiO2 interference', but blames the disagreement mainly on acquisition and focus and never describes the rise to about 4 layers followed by a fall.

It warns that 'Substrate, strain, charge doping, laser heating… can all move A1g and E2g differently, so Δ alone is a layer estimate', but gives no strain coefficients and does not say that electron doping softens and broadens A1g.

The widths are reported (A1g FWHM A 6.4, B 4.9, D 4.6, C 2.9; E2g about 2.1 in all four), but the report treats A's width as an anomaly from strain or terraces rather than stating that A1g is broader in few-layer flakes than in the thick one.
It uses the Si line as an internal reference ('Si reads 520.0 instead of 520.7'), corrects for the offset, and asks 'Was the wavenumber axis calibrated (for example to Si or a neon line)?'

wrong_claims.why: It explicitly says 'Absolute MoS2 intensities give no reliable thickness ordering' and does not assign layers from intensity.
It describes E2g as higher and A1g as lower on the monolayer side, and Δ as increasing with thickness.
The 265.09 cm⁻¹ point is identified as 'a single-point cosmic-ray spike' and removed before fitting.

items.why: The report fits the band with separate components, "2LA(M) at 351.09 cm-1 (FWHM 8.9...); E2g^1 at 355.28 cm-1 ... a shoulder on the high-frequency side of the 2LA band", using three-Lorentzian fits.

It gives intensity ratios against E2g, not A1g ("about 9.6 on spot 1 ... about 1.7 on spot 2"), and says the 2LA band "dominates" on spot 1 and is "a minor shoulder" on spot 2, so the resonance contrast is there but the 2LA/A1g ratio fingerprint (>2 vs ~0.5) is never stated.
"A1g is 417.28 vs 420.08, a 2.8 cm-1 downshift on spot 1", with spot 1 read as monolayer-compatible and spot 2 as thick.
"Separation 62.00 cm-1" for spot 1 and "64.70 cm-1" for spot 2, obtained after fitting E2g separately from 2LA(M).

It says "the separation alone cannot separate 1L from 2L" and only assumes spot 2 is "several to tens of layers", but it never states that the steps between 2L, 3L and bulk are ~1 cm-1, i.e. that positions weakly constrain layer number beyond the monolayer.
It checks the Si line against 520.7 cm-1 ("offset of +0.1–0.2 cm-1"), asks about calibration, and links 2LA(M) strength to resonance at 514.5 nm near the B exciton.

wrong_claims.why: E2g is fitted as a separate shoulder at 355.3 cm-1, distinct from the 2LA maximum at 351.1, and the separation is built on that fitted E2g.
2LA(M) is assigned as a "two-phonon overtone, resonantly enhanced", and the report states "No defect-activated band ... is evident".

items.why: The report says doses 1–3 are "stage 1 (isolated point defects)". It gives G FWHM "14.0, 13.9, 13.9", sharp monolayer 2D (FWHM 32, I_2D/I_G ~3), and rising D and D' heights (D 702→2046→2971; D' 119→331→433).

From peak heights at 532 nm it gets I_D/I_G "0.250 -> 0.569 -> 1.191" and L_D "23.9, 15.5 and 10.3 nm", all inside the rubric ranges. It used the Lucchese-form C_A=160/E_L^4 model rather than Eq. 4 by name.

It applies the wavelength scaling explicitly ("E_L = 2.331 eV; C_A = 160/E_L^4"). It never says the same ratio gives a different L_D at another laser line. Its question about whether "the 514.5 nm dataset ... applies unchanged" muddles the point.

For dose 4 it reports "D/G falling back to 0.58", G FWHM 45 vs 14, "2D band lost", and D' overlapping the G shoulder. It concludes dose 4 is "past the maximum ... on the high-density branch" (L_D ~1.2 nm) and that the stage-1 relation cannot be applied.

It gives "I_D/I_D' is about 6-7 across doses 1-3" as "closest to the vacancy-like value" and quotes Eckmann's 13/7/3.5. It does not say the classification holds only in the low-density regime; it calls dose 4 unreliable only because D' is weak.

It states "I used peak heights" and reports the area ratios that differ. It also says "Whether the source model uses heights or areas was not verified", so it never ties Cancado's calibration to heights.

It asks for the dose "in physical units (ion fluence, plasma time, or similar)", but only for cross-calibration. It does not link the treatment type to the point-defect assumption or to the D/D' defect-type dependence.

wrong_claims.why: It says dose 4 is on the high-density branch and that Eq. 4 is not valid for it ("no defect density can be given"), and it gives no L_D above 10 nm.
It uses E_L = 2.331 eV (532 nm) with E_L^-4 scaling, not the 514.5 nm constants.
It calls the spike near 2150 cm^-1 "a single-point spike ... an artifact" and does not analyse it.

items.why: The report says both peaks "red-shift monotonically with laser power; the Si 520 cm-1 reference does not shift". It also reports power broadening ("G FWHM 13.9, 15.9, 18.0") and concludes the shifts are "a laser-power effect on one spot, not a sample difference" that "fits local laser heating".

It uses chi_G = -0.016 and chi_2D = -0.034 and finds "dT_G ... about 112 K and dT_2D ... about 151 K for 5 mW relative to 0.5 mW", which is roughly in range. However, it gives no 2 mW estimate and calls the G and 2D estimates "inconsistent" rather than consistent.

It computes the 2D/G slope ratio (2.71–2.85) and compares it with the "~2.1 temperature-coefficient ratio and the ~2.2 strain ratio". It never says that a naive Lee-style G vs 2D analysis would misread the heating trajectory as strain.
It says to "Trust the 0.5 mW spectrum for positions", cites the zero-power extrapolation, and says "The 2 and 5 mW spectra are useful only as a power series for the heating correction."
It asks "Can you measure a power series down to about 0.1 mW" to pin the zero-power reference and asks to confirm power at the sample, but it never asks about spot size or power density.

It uses the 0.5 mW spectrum as the reference (G 1581.30, 2D 2669.52) and reports "no doping signature". But rather than calling it close to pristine, it suggests the 2D near 2670 "would hint at tensile strain or residual doping" and leaves strain undetermined.

wrong_claims.why: It attributes the power-dependent shifts to heating, not strain or doping; doping is explicitly rejected ("shifts go the wrong way for doping").
It recommends the 0.5 mW spectrum, not the highest-power one.

items.why: The report states "Both spectra are graphene" and gives G at 1580.4 and 2D at 2680.9 cm-1 on Au, and G at 1581.0 and 2D at 2695.6 cm-1 on Cu.

It gives D at 1344 cm-1 on Au and 1349.6 cm-1 on Cu, with "Au ... ID/IG about 0.97 (heights); Cu ... ID/IG about 0.62 +/- 0.27", and flags the Cu value as poorly constrained ("about 1.3 sigma, so it is not established").

The report puts the difference down to "metal-specific graphene-metal coupling" and to possible carbon precipitation on cooling; it never offers strain from rapid solidification as the authors' explanation for the stronger D on Au.

It treats ID/IG as a defect level and says strain is "Not separable" without a reference, noting the G shift does not resolve whether the 2D upshift is strain. It never says outright that D needs defects or edges to appear, or that a strain explanation for D should be checked against the G and 2D positions.

It asks "What laser wavelength was used? It sets the D and 2D reference positions, the L_D relation..." and notes in the caveats that D and 2D disperse with excitation energy; its L_D relation uses lambda^4.

It notes "The Cu spectrum is near the detection limit: G height about 3 times the point noise, D about 2.6 sigma", gives error bars on the Cu ratios, and points out that both spectra are single acquisitions with no repeat.

wrong_claims.why: Although the summary says no defect distance can be stated, the properties list "L_D about 11 nm (514 nm), 12 nm (532 nm), 17 nm (633 nm) for Au, conditional on the laser wavelength", which are quantitative L_D values given without a known wavelength.
The report never says the D peak on Au is caused by strain; it brings in strain only for the 2D width and the Cu 2D shift, and only as possibilities.

items.why: The report measures flake 2 at 1368.96 cm⁻¹ versus 1366.20 cm⁻¹ for flake 1 ("+2.76 ± 0.25 cm⁻¹"), says this is "in the range Gorbachev et al. (2011) associate with a monolayer", and reports a broader FWHM (22.2 vs 17.99 cm⁻¹).
It states "Gorbachev (2011) reports up to 4 cm⁻¹ with ±2 cm⁻¹ sample scatter" and calls the upshift "not an unambiguous monolayer marker".
It says "substrate strain and sample-to-sample scatter produce similar shifts" but never mentions the typical 1–2 cm⁻¹ red shifts from cleavage strain or that they dominate in bilayers.

It notes the much weaker hBN signal ("much thinner than flake 1 in terms of hBN signal") and a linear I ∝ N law that needs calibration, but it calls the intensity unusable here ("cannot be converted to a layer count") and favours the shear mode, rather than presenting intensity as the more useful layer measure.

It asks for AFM height ("the most decisive check"), cites the optical-contrast method with the 80 ± 10 nm SiO2 optimum, and asks for a bare SiO2/Si reference to normalise intensities against the Si line.

wrong_claims.why: The report says "a monolayer is possible but unconfirmed" and "Layer number is not determined".
The report never says a bilayer is upshifted like a monolayer; it only gives "1 to a few layers" as a range.

items.why: The report gives day2−day1 shifts of "E2g +2.507, A1g +2.439" cm-1 and says the "E2g-A1g separation is unchanged between days" at about 21.5–21.6 cm-1.
It reports the "Si line 519.976 ... (d1) vs 522.469 ... (d2)" and concludes "the shift is a rigid calibration offset" rather than a change in the flake.
After Si referencing, "E2g and A1g positions agree to about 0.02 cm-1" (A1g −0.06, within uncertainty), and the ~21.5 cm-1 separation is "closest to the 2-layer value" on both days.

It states "electron doping would soften A1g", that strain "would shift E2g and change the splitting; neither changed", and that "Peak widths are unchanged within error". It does not mention A1g broadening explicitly, but the physics matches.
It asks "Was the spectrometer recalibrated or the grating/centre wavelength changed between the two days?" and "Was there a Si reference (or a Ne/Hg lamp line) measured on each day?"

wrong_claims.why: The report rejects adsorbate doping and strain: "that shift is spectrometer calibration, not doping or strain."
It reports no change in layer number or crystal quality; widths are "unchanged" and the layer count is the same (about 2) on both days.

items.why: The report states that the 'E2g softens and A1g hardens from B to C' and that Δ grows with thickness, citing Lee et al.: 'E2g frequency decreases and the A1g frequency increases with thickness'.

The measured Δ values match (B 19.23, A 21.46 cm-1), but the report assigns 'B ≈ 1–2 layers, A ≈ 3–4 layers', which puts A at the wrong layer count, and it claims 'Δ alone cannot separate 1 L from 2 L', which contradicts the rubric's point that the 1L-to-2L step is the most robust distinction.

It calls C (25.06) and D (24.27) 'bulk-like (at least about 5 layers, not resolvable further)', which captures that they can only be bounded, not counted, but it sets the bound at 5 rather than about 4 layers and declines to name C as the thicker flake ('cannot be ranked against each other with confidence').

It says absolute intensities 'do not indicate thickness' and lists 'flake/substrate interference' as one cause, but it never describes the non-monotonic interference behaviour (intensity rising to about 4 layers and then falling, monolayer stronger than bulk).

It warns that 'strain, doping (electron doping softens A1g)... can shift the two modes by fractions to about 1 cm-1' and that this could move B relative to A, but it gives no strain coefficient (about 4.5 cm-1/% for E', A' nearly unchanged) and does not mention doping-induced broadening.
It reports 'E2g 2.06–2.21 cm-1 in all four; A1g FWHM A 6.6, B 5.0, D 4.6, C 3.1 cm-1', so A1g is broadest in A (the rubric's bilayer) and narrowest in the thick flake C, while E2g stays about 2 cm-1.
It applies a per-flake Si correction ('520.7 − measured Si = +0.68 ... cm-1') and asks 'Do you have a reference Si spectrum taken on the same instrument to set the absolute calibration?'.

wrong_claims.why: Layer numbers come from Δ; the report says intensities 'do not indicate thickness', and it treats the Si/E2g ratio only as 'weak evidence only'.
The report states the correct direction: E2g softens with thickness and Δ grows.
It identifies the 265.09 cm-1 point in C as a 'cosmic-ray artifact' and removes it by interpolation before fitting.

items.why: The report quotes a separate "2LA/E2g area ratio 9 vs 1.8", which implies it fitted the two modes separately, but it never says the 350–356 cm-1 band is two overlapping modes or gives their positions (about 351 and 355 cm-1).

It shows 2LA(M) much stronger at spot 1 ("2LA/E2g area ratio 9 vs 1.8"), but it uses E2g, not A1g, as the reference and never gives the 2LA/A1g ratio above 2 vs about 0.5 or calls it the monolayer fingerprint.

It reports "A1g 417.28 vs 420.08 cm-1", which matches the rubric numbers, but it only concludes "Spot 1 looks thinner" and says "monolayer status not established" instead of linking the shift to monolayer vs bulk.
The report never gives the A1g minus E2g1 separation for either spot.
It never says the position steps between 2L, 3L and bulk are only about 1 cm-1; "No layer count claimed" gives no physical reason.
It mentions Si only as a height indicator ("Si net height 1235 vs 118 counts"), not as a calibration check, and its only question is about PL, not the laser line or resonance.

wrong_claims.why: It never assigns the band maximum to E2g1 alone or builds a layer count on that position or separation; it states "No layer count claimed."
It never calls 2LA(M) a defect or impurity peak.
